newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Klerk knew of covert operations, assassin says.
newsitem.headline: De Klerk knew of covert operations, assassin says.

text.p: F.W. de Klerk, leader of South Africa's opposition National Party, knew of covert state military units that operated while he was president, an apartheid-era assassin said on Wednesday.

"De Klerk cannot say he did not know that such (covert) organisations existed. He gave the order for the attack on the Transkei in 1993," Eugene de Kock told a court where he is pleading for leniency after conviction for murder.

"Who did he think was going to carry out that attack? He certainly knew there were covert organisations," said de Kock, former commander of a covert death squad unit set up by the apartheid government.

Some children died in an attack in 1993 on a house in the Transkei, a nominally independent homeland. The incident nearly derailed government-opposition negotiations that brought democracy the next year.

De Klerk apologised for apartheid last month and acknowledged that his and previous governments had approved "unconventional" actions which "created the environment within which abuses and gross violations of human rights could take place".

"Within my knowledge and experience (these actions) never included the authorisation of assassination, murder, torture, rape, assault or the like," he added. "Nor did I individually directly or indirectly ever suggest, order or authorise any such action."
